To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the AC losses are very small and can be neglected in the design of current leads; 2) the critical current of stacks is higher than that of single tape; 3) the critical current decreases with increasing the magnetic field, but it is still higher than that of a single tape at the field of 0.5 tesla.

The AC loss in the stack is proportional to the square of the current amplitude, and it is almost independent on the frequency in the range 10 Hz - 100 Hz, and that the AC loss in the stacks is almost independent of the magnetic field in the range 0.05 T - 0.5T.
the AC loss in the stacks can be minimized by optimizing the tape overlap length.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the electrical properties of stacks of Bi-2223 superconducting tapes, with the aim of developing HTS current leads for particle accelerators.
the characterization of HTS tapes and the development of a model for the calculation of critical current and AC losses of stacks of tapes.
the study of AC losses in Bi-2223 stacks, with particular attention on the effect of the number of tapes and of the current density distribution on the AC loss behavior.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
stacks of BSCCO tape are very suitable for use in current leads for LHC.
stacks of BSCCO tapes represent the most suitable HTS conductor for the LHC current leads, as far as the current and the field are limited to the values of practical interest.

, although the AC loss is higher than the DC loss for a stack of tapes, the difference is not large and, therefore, the use of HTS stacks is still an attractive option for the design of LHC current leads.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the AC losses of stacks of BSCCO tapes can be reduced by increasing the number of tapes, but only up to a certain number, which is dependent on the critical current density of the individual tapes.
we have demonstrated the feasibility of using stacks of HTS tapes as current leads for the LHC.

we have shown that the Bi-2222 stacks are a viable alternative to the conventional CuNi conductors, and that they have a great potential in terms of reduction of the heat losses in the leads, with the additional advantage of a reduced weight.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the critical current and AC loss values are strongly dependent on the number of tapes in the stack, on the current distribution among the tapes, on the tape length, and on the magnetic field.
the stacks of Bi-2223 conductors can provide a high critical current and very low AC losses in the operating conditions of the LHC current leads.
the critical current of the stacks is limited by the critical current of individual tape, while the AC losses are dominated by the tape-to-tape contact resistance.
